sections.markdown:
This skill allows Moonveil's wielder to assume a sheathed Iaido-style stance which is then followed up by two unique slashing attacks. The Light Attack triggers a wide horizontal slash, releasing an arc-shaped magic projectile attack. The Heavy Attack triggers a vertical downward slash, also releasing a similar projectile attack. Both projectiles take the form of a medium range blue arc, which can be aimed freely; useful when dealing with large enemies with weak points above standard striking level, such as dragon heads.

While Moonveil itself deals split physical (slashing) and magical damage, the beam released from this skill deals strictly magical damage. - The Light Attack is excellent for crowd control against hoards of low-poise enemies.
- Wearing Spellblade Set increases the damage
- Damage of the waves fired is 100% Magic Damage and is affected by Intelligence but not Dexterity or Strength.
- This skill activates and benefits from Rellana's Cameo talisman.
- This Skill deals 12.5 Poise damage with the magic projectile using either variant.
 - A direct hit from the Moonveil used to fire it will do an additional 15 using the Light Attack variant for a total of 27.5 Poise damage.
 - The Heavy Attack variant deals an additional 17.5 with the Katana itself for a total of 30 Poise damage on a direct strike.
- This Skill is not Chargeable
- This Skill's Light and Heavy attacks can be Parried
- The projectiles can be parried using Golden Retaliation, Ash of War: Carian Retaliation and the Carian Retaliation sorcery.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
Vitality** is a resistance stat in Elden Ring.

Vitality governs the Tarnished's ability to resist the build-up of Death Blight.

The Tarnished's base Focus is the sum total of two different parts, with each part determined by their Level and Arcane attribute. The first part is calculated based on the Tarnished's level. Their Vitality will increase as they level up, with soft caps at level 71, 111 and 161. The second part is calculated based off of the Tarnished's Arcane stat. The total of these two parts is what is displayed on the status screen.

Raising Arcane to increase Vitality has soft caps at 15, 40 and 60.
- From 1-15 Arcane: +1 Vitality each level
- From 16-40 Arcane: +0.6 Vitality each level
- From 41-60 Arcane: +0.5 Vitality each level
- From 61-99 Arcane: +0.25 Vitality each level

Vitality is further increased by equipping armor, which will display in the righthand column of the Status screen.

sections.heading: Recreating
sections.markdown:
Though this beta origin is mostly available in the form of the release version of the Warrior, some equipment has been changed.

The weapons, shield, and ash of war are acquirable in Limgrave: Scimitars can be gained by killing Scimitar-wielding Skeletons at a 2% drop rate (Deathtouched Catacombs is the earliest farming spot) or 1 can be bought from Twin Maiden Husks for 600 Runes or 2 are held by the Warrior Origin as starting equipment, Buckler can be gained by buying it from Gatekeeper Gostoc for 1,500 Runes or by starting as a Bandit, and 1 Ash of War: Storm Blade can be bought from Bernahl at Warmaster's Shack (getting a second one requires a Lost Ashes of War, easiest gained by buying from either the Isolated Merchant at the Isolated Merchant's Shack (Weeping Peninsula) or the Isolated Merchant hidden in Academy of Raya Lucaria).

The Blue Cloth Set can be gained by either starting as a Warrior or bought from the Isolated Merchant hidden in Academy of Raya Lucaria and found by going around the eastern transportation sigil at the Main Academy Gate Site of Grace.

sections.heading: Suitable Origins
sections.markdown:
The Warrior is obviously extremely suitable, seeing as it only lacks the Buckler and Ash of War: Storm Blade to have the whole kit.

The Bandit Origin has the shield starting out, can gain the rest of the important equipment relatively easily, and has the stats to use all of it.

The Prisoner, Samurai, and Vagabond Origins also have the stats to use the equipment by default.

After observing that Golden Order Fundamentalism could not alleviate his sister's sickness, Miquella began pursuing other means of treating her condition. One of these pursuits leading to the creation of Unalloyed Gold, a substance that Miquella would make into a primary design element in the equipment of his army and closest companions.

Repeatedly used as a medium to compel affection and raise faith, one of the primary inventions that enforced the pursuit of this metal were the many prototypes of Miquella's Needle. An artifact that when inserted into ones flesh, had the ability to ward away the meddling of the outer gods. However, even the latest and most advanced model of these needles are still considered incomplete, and could only accomplish this fully if inserted into the flesh while standing in a location that has been untouched by time, the only currently known location being the heart of the storm found in Farum Azula.

sections.markdown: Thiollier** is an NPC merchant in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
A Tarnished, Thiollier was an isolated young man who encountered St. Trina, just once, and was granted the sweet repose of velvety sleep. The remainder of his days would be spent in search of the means to recapture it, despite Miquella's enchantment. He views himself as utterly weak and useless, though he is, in secret, an expert in the realm of mixing poisons. He wears a mask with a tranquil sleeping face carved on it, its silver hair is arranged in the same style as St. Trina's, increasing arcane. Additionally, he has sewn countless needles onto the exterior of his garb for a talismanic effect.

Thiollier touched Miquella's withered arm at the Cocoon of the Empyrean and, alongside other followers of Miquella, entered the Realm of Shadow after the death of Mohg, Lord of Blood. The player Tarnished can help Thiollier create a condensed, somniferous elixir, purported to be capable of putting even an ancient dragon to sleep, although fatal for any mortal. Should his questline be completed, Thiollier can see St. Trina once more in the Garden of Deep Purple.

sections.heading: Location
sections.markdown: Thiollier sits by himself, quite some distance from his compatriots, at the Pillar Path Cross Site of Grace, located on the northeastern border of the Gravesite Plain. He later moves to the Garden of Deep Purple. Thiollier can be summoned as a cooperator against Putrescent Knight, Miquella's Followers, and Promised Consort Radahn.

- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage.

- The skill, Mists of Eternal Sleep, has two parts. The second is a Weapon Buff that increases the sword's innate Eternal Sleep build-up by 15 for 30 seconds.

- Scales best with Dexterity, but unlike with the Sword of St. Trina the Strength- and Intelligence-scaling isn't far behind, and its base Magic damage is far greater. This means that the sword deals roughly equal amounts of damage on a hybrid Strength/Dexterity build, a pure Dexterity build, and a hybrid Dexterity/Intelligence build.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **War of the Ancient Dragons**, refers to the conflict in the Lands Between between the forces of Leyndell and the Ancient Dragons.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
During the reign of Queen Marika the Eternal and Godfrey, the first Elden Lord, at some point after the end of the Age of Plenty the royal capital of Leyndell was attacked by Ancient Dragon Gransax.

The immense dragon wielding a giant golden spear managed to fell the walls of Leyndell for the first time in recorded history and wreck havoc upon the city until it was finally defeated, his massive corpse left lying between the Fortified Manor and the lower city. Gransax's assault marked the beginning of the War against the Ancient Dragons.

For the battles to come, the priests of the Erdtree would develop incantations to protect the knights of Leyndell against the lightning of the dragons.

sections.heading: Battles
sections.markdown:
The dragon's attack on the capital caused some among the Tree Sentinels, the guardians of the Erdtree, to have an epiphany; According to them, the only way to protect the Erdtree was to become dragons themselves. Thus, some of the Sentinels began to emulate the Ancient Dragons in order to provide proper protection for the Erdtree against the new threat. They adorned their armor with dragon imagery and wielding weapons and shields imbued with red lightning, crafted whittling from the claws of great dragon that fell on their city. From then on, these grotesque Tree Sentinels are referred to as Draconic Tree Sentinels.

The last battle of the war happened in the Altus Plateau, outside the outer walls of Leyndell. Godwyn the Golden, the son of Queen Marika and Lord Godfrey, engaged in conflict against Ancient Dragon Fortissax, who had stood out during the war for its usage of twin red lightning stakes and was known as the "mightiest boulderstone".

Fighting with courage, Godwyn triumphed over Fortissax before eventually befriending him and sparing his life. This event marked the end of the war against the Ancient Dragons and their integration into the Golden Order.

sections.heading: Aftermath
sections.markdown:
Through his friendship with Fortissax, Godwyn learned to channel golden lightning. and their bond gave rise to the Ancient Dragon Cult in Leyndell. The dragon cult worshiped the ancient dragons and their incantations channeled lightning instead of the power of the Erdtree, but these practices were sanctioned by the Golden Order, as lightning and the Gravel Stones of the dragons were imbued with gold.

The cultists devotedly worshipped the Ancient Dragons and prayed for their golden lightning incantations thus adding another great power to Leyndell's arsenal, although the red-hued incantations remained a secret of Farum Azula, as its prayerbooks never reached the rest of the Lands Between.

Ancient Dragon Lansseax, the sister of Fortissax, assumed a human form and became the priestess for the Dragon Cult of Leyndell to interact with its knights. Only those loved by the dragons could receive the blessing of their lightning and survive their lightning, with Vyke the Dragonspear being the most favored by Lansseax and able to imbue his body even with red lightning.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- It is possible that during the war, battles between Leyndell forces and Dragons happened even in Crumbling Farum Azula.
 - The Golden Lightning Fortification incantation used during the war is obtained from a scarab rolling the ashes left on the ruined city
 - Golden Runes from 9 to 12, those of people born at the foot of the Erdtree and those of people that first served it, can be found on the ruined city.
 - Two Crucible Knights can still be found fighting Beastmen in the ruined city.
- It is possible that, in the last battle of the war, Demigods or nobles closely affiliated with the Golden Lineage fought and died.
 - The Sainted Hero's Grave, built close to the site of the last battle, implies that champions of holy status were buried in the catacomb.
 - The banners found on the Sainted Hero's Grave display the symbol of the Golden Lineage.
 - Godwyn was the first Demigod to die in "recorded history".

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Thorn sorceries**, also known as **aberrant sorceries**, are a type of sorcery in Elden Ring. These Faith-based spells damage the caster to summon cursed Briars of Sin that deal Magic damage and inflict Blood Loss upon their targets. Drawn from the heretical blood star and the forsaken Scadutree, thorn sorceries reflect the agonizing woe of those who wield them.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Thorn sorceries, encompassing both bloodthorn hexes and impenetrable thorn sorceries, embody the torment of their casters. Bloodthorn hexes summon spiraling tendrils of blood, born from the suffering of those who beheld the blood star after their eyes were crushed by the Briars. These guilty sorcerers use smoldering saplings as a catalyst to transform sacrificial blood into red glintstone, a practice reviled by the sorcerers of the Academy of Raya Lucaria.

Impenetrable thorn sorceries, in contrast, are tied to the holiness of the sacred Scadutree. They were created by those who abandoned incantations after their devout Faith led only to despair. Both forms of thorn sorcery channel the anguish of those condemned by Queen Marika.

sections.heading: Boosting thorn sorceries
sections.markdown:
Briars of Punishment, Briars of Sin, and Impenetrable Thorns:
- Alberich's Bracers, Alberich's Robe, Alberich's Pointed Hat, and Alberich's Pointed Hat (Altered) each boost the effectiveness of Briars of Punishment, Briars of Sin, and Impenetrable Thorns by 6%.
- Staff of the Guilty boosts the Attack Power of Briars of Punishment, Briars of Sin, and Impenetrable Thorns by 20%.
- Magic Scorpion Charm increases Magic Attack Power by 12% (8% in PvP).
- Magic-Shrouding Cracked Tear increases Magic Attack Power by 20% (15% in PvP) for 3 minutes.
- Albinauric Staff and Maternal Staff provide a scaling bonus to Blood Loss buildup based on the caster's Arcane attribute.
- Azur's Glintstone Staff reduces the casting time of sorceries.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Alberich's Robe (Altered) and Alberich's Trousers do not provide a bonus to thorn sorceries.
- Mantle of Thorns does not benefit from effects that boost thorn sorceries but provides considerable damage when rolling, especially when combined with the Briar Armor set.
- Thorn sorceries do not produce a spell sigil when cast.
- Wielded by the Guilty and the mysterious Scadutree Avatars.
- Thorn sorceries impale their targets from below.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- There are four thorn sorceries in total.
- Mad Tongue Alberich was tormented into madness by his fellows at the Roundtable Hold long ago. He wielded cold sorceries and devoted himself to the red glintstone.
- The Man-Serpents of Mt. Gelmir use their faith to cast lava sorcery with red glintstone as the catalyst.
- The Briars of Sin had a different icon during the Closed Network Test for Elden Ring. It featured the spell sigil for Giants' Flame Incantations.

sections.markdown: This page lists **Trees** in Elden Ring, Shadow of the Erdtree, and Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Trees held deep symbolic and spiritual importance to the people of the Lands Between and the Realm of Shadow, particularly to groups like the Woodfolk. The greatest of these trees were suffused with profound holiness, bestowing sacred blessings in the form of soaring grace, Golden Dew, and blessed sap, which dripped from their boughs and hardened into Crystal Tears and treasured amber. These great trees typically grew from potent sources of life energy. For example, Queen Marika used the Crucible to create her Erdtree, and Miquella watered the doomed Haligtree with his divine Empyrean blood. Certain trees manifested stylized avatars to protect themselves and their offspring in times of need. The Erdtree could rebirth or renew its followers through esoteric death rites like Erdtree Burial.

Some individuals gained the power of trees by channeling aspects of the Crucible or by entering pacts with great trees. For example, the Tree Guardians received eternal life to defend the Erdtree and its offspring; the end of their service was said to approach when their buds bloom into blood-red flowers, beginning their slow transformation into trees.

However, the all-female, blind shamans—spirited-away denizens of another world—and their descendants, the Numen, inherently possessed the greatest arboreal affinity in all the Lands Between. Their founding Grandmother formed a small yet significant tree at the Shaman Village, Marika's home, long ago. The flesh of shamans was later prized for its ability to graft and meld harmoniously with that of others. Many maidens were dismembered to create jar saints, while others bulged from inside trees around Enir-Ilim.

Feminine forms likewise manifested in other trees related to Marika or her people, including the motherly womb at the Haligtree Roots and the praying maiden bound by a Cord End inside a blossom sealed within Limveld's secret cave. Just as dried prunings from the Erdtree were snapped in lieu of death, the Cutting-Gifted Tribe atoned for learning the original sin by offering up their young maidens to become Sacrificial Twigs.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Many trees on the Mountaintops of the Giants have become spirits.
- The bodies and souls of warriors who receive Erdtree Burial are absorbed by the Erdtree. Art in the catacombs suggests this practice causes new or reborn life to later sprout from the Erdtree.
- There is a unique "root tree" in the courtyard of the Shadow Keep, Church District.
- Bleached willow trees are commonly found throughout the realm of shadow, especially in areas associated with the hornsent.
- , such as those found in Altus Plateau, can regrow their bark once peeled off. The Secret Rite Scroll, which details the Gate of Divinity's workings, was recorded on birch bark.
- Fallen red oak and maple leaves blanket the land at Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree and the Scadutree Chalice.
- Fallen oak leaves litter the Deeproot Depths, especially around the hollowed-out tree guarded by Crucible Knight Siluria.
- The Cutting-Gifted Tribe converted their maidens to Sacrificial Twigs to atone for learning the Erdtree's Original Sin. The bound figure in Limveld's secret room is possibly connected to the divine Spirit Shelter.

sections.markdown: The **Thrusting Counterattack** is a gameplay mechanic in Elden Ring and Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: Thrusting Counterattacks are special Guard Counters that deal bonus damage, unique to weapons that deal Pierce damage. Like Guard Counters, they are peformed after Guarding an attack; however, they must strike the target during one of its attack animations to inflict the bonus damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Only weapons that deal Pierce damage can perform Thrusting Counterattacks. The weapon no longer counts for Thrusting Counterattacks if its damage is fully converted to a different damage type.
- The simplified UI in *Nightreign* hides the physical damage types, making it difficult to determine which weapons count in the field.
